### 💡 Codex Review https://github.com/Patricked-code/MCP/blob/160506ee60906ead8a3c04c25e49d449023cb1d0/src/evidence/githubReadonlyRoutes.ts#L138 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Fit sequential health checks within the route timeout** When one or more endpoints are slow or unreachable, these three sequential transfers can consume up to 30 seconds: `curl --help all` defines `--max-time` as the maximum time allowed per transfer. However, the OIDC route invokes `runReadOnlyCommand` with a 15-second timeout in `src/server.ts`, and the workflow client itself has a 20-second timeout, so the probe can be aborted before emitting all three status lines—precisely when outage evidence is needed. Run the requests concurrently, reduce their individual limits, or increase both enclosing timeouts. --- https://github.com/Patricked-code/MCP/blob/160506ee60906ead8a3c04c25e49d449023cb1d0/src/evidence/githubReadonlyRoutes.ts#L122 **![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat) Filter Stablecoin processes before truncating the PID list** On an S2 host with more than 80 matching Passenger or Node processes, `head -n 80` truncates the global PID set before the subsequent `comm`/`cwd` Stablecoin filter. (`pgrep --help` confirms that `-f` matches the full process name.) A Stablecoin worker outside those first 80 entries is therefore omitted, and the reconciliation artifact can falsely suggest that no application process is running; apply the limit after filtering or narrow the initial selection to the Stablecoin paths.
